land.text: the centre and north of the peninsula that Kung Ye took from Silla and from the local lords: 'almost two-thirds of the land once controlled by Silla' (Gungye page)

predecessors.note: Cliopatria keeps all of it in the Unified Silla row until 910 and starts Taebong in 911.

land.text: the whole of Taebong, taken over in the coup of 918

successors.note: Wang Kon 'restored the name Goryeo'; the Taebong page says Kung Ye's state was first called Goryeo too, so Goryeo is arguably the same state under a new ruler.

capitals.name: Songak (Kaesong)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Songak (898)'; the Gungye page puts his rebellion at present-day Kaesong in 898 and does not name Songak. The state is dated from 901.

capitals.name: Cheorwon
capitals.note: Kung Ye 'moved the capital to Cheorwon' in 905 (Taebong and Gungye pages). Coordinates are the county seat; the gazetteer has no Cheorwon entry.

rulers.name: Gungye (Kung Ye)
rulers.note: Footnote: 'reigned from July 901 until 14 June 918' in the lunisolar calendar; overthrown by four generals who enthroned Wang Kon.

correction.text: Songak/Kaesong and the central Korean lords Kung Ye defeated

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the page dates the state to 901 ('established by Kung Ye ... in 901') but Cliopatria starts Taebong in 911. Before 905 the pages date no conquest; Kung Ye 'instigated his own rebellion in present-day Kaesong in 898' and beat Yang Kil and other local lords of central Korea before 901. The core is therefore a 100 km circle round Kaesong (confidence 1).

New keyframe: 'In 905 ... Kung Ye took over Pyongyang' and he held 'almost two-thirds of the land once controlled by Silla', Chungcheong included. Cliopatria draws this outline from 911 (81,790 km2) and keeps it inside Unified Silla until 910. The Taebong page gives no area; its map caption says 'at its height in 915'.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 911 outline plus Naju; valid 911-917

keyframe_review.note: 81,790 km2 for 911-921. The page ends the state in 918 (the Goryeo years 918-921 are goryeo_918). In 910 Wang Kon 'attacked and captured the city of Naju' (Gyeon Hwon page), which lies south of the Cliopatria outline (southern limit 36.03 N) and inside Hubaekje's.

region.text: Songak/Kaesong, where Kung Ye rebelled in 898 and absorbed Wang Kon's forces

ledger.note: 901: Kung Ye proclaims Later Goguryeo. 'a state established by Kung Ye on the Korean Peninsula in 901' (Taebong page; infobox 901-918); Gungye page: he 'proclaim[ed] himself king of Later Goguryeo' in 901 after his 898 rebellion at Kaesong. Taebong page: 'The state's initial name was Goryeo.'
904: the kingdom is renamed Majin 'after a suggestion by Ajitae' (Taebong page; Gungye page: 'changed the country's name to Majin in 904').
905: the capital moves to Cheorwon ('Kung Ye moved the capital to Cheorwon' in 905).

905: Kung Ye takes Pyongyang. 'In 905 ... Kung Ye took over Pyongyang and called for total destruction of the state of Silla.' No state is named as the loser; counterpart unified-silla (reviewer jk-02-c, was nobody) because about two-thirds of this 100 km circle lies inside Cliopatria's Unified Silla 892 outline, which the unified-silla dossier keeps to 904, and the page has the aristocrats of Paeseo submitting and Kung Ye holding 'almost two-thirds of the land once controlled by Silla'.

region.text: the centre and north taken from Silla's realm, outside the Kaesong and Pyongyang cores

ledger.note: c.905: Kung Ye holds 'almost two-thirds of the land once controlled by Silla', including Chungcheong; 'Myeongju and Paeseo local aristocrats submitted to him'. The page dates none of it except Pyongyang (905); the year is a bridge from the Pyongyang entry.

910: Wang Kon takes Naju. 'In 910, Wang Kŏn attacked and captured the city of Naju. Kyŏn later failed to retake it after a ten-day siege.' The page does not say who held it before; Hubaekje is read as the loser because Kyŏn Hwŏn tried to retake it.
911: the kingdom takes the name Taebong ('He changed the name of his kingdom to Taebong in 911').

region.text: all of Taebong, passing whole to Goryeo

ledger.note: 918: four generals overthrow Kung Ye and enthrone Wang Kon, who restores the name Goryeo. 'Four generals (Hong Yu, Pae Hyŏngyŏng, Sin Sunggyŏm, Pok Chigyŏm) overthrew T'aebong in 918'; the Gungye footnote gives the end of his reign as 14 June 918 (lunisolar) and his death as 24 July 918. Goryeo's own infobox has the coronation on 25 July 918.

wars.name: Later Three Kingdoms (Taebong phase)
wars.outcome: Kung Ye took the centre and north from Silla; the state fell to its own generals in 918, not to a rival.
wars.note: The pages give no dated battle; the 910 capture of Naju is a ledger event.

certainty.note: No frontier is dated or described on the pages; every border of the state is approximate.

notes: Cliopatria's Taebong row (911-921, one shape of 81,790 km2) has four problems: the pages date the state to 901-918, not 911-921; Goryeo's own row starts in 922 with the same outline; the Unified Silla row keeps the north to 910. Fixes in taebong_901/905, unified-silla_905 and goryeo_918. No infobox area on the Taebong page, so the Cliopatria area could not be compared. Taebong and Goryeo may be one state (Kung Ye's kingdom was first called Goryeo and Wang Kon restored the name after a coup); they are two dossiers here because Cliopatria has two rows and the pages call Taebong a separate state: the colour agent should give them one hue family. 918 month: the Gungye footnote's 14 June is lunisolar, Goryeo's infobox 25 July 918 is not, so the months are only ordered, not exact. Pages: 3 opened against a budget of 1-2 (Gyeon Hwon added for the 910 Naju capture, which is also the matching event for Hubaekje's loss). Naju is missing from the gazetteer (list for the gazetteer agent); Cheorwon too.
